How the ratings work

Every distinct date is one Glicko-2 rating period, so each rating change maps to the games played that day. Regular season and postseason games all count (switch any of them off in Settings).

Between seasons the rating carries over and the rating deviation (RD) resets to a smaller starting value, since the team's history is informative. If a franchise disappeared, all continuing teams are moved by the same amount so the league average is back at 1500. A new franchise enters at the rating that keeps the league average at 1500 (Settings lets you choose between that literal rule and first re-centring the continuing teams so entrants come in at exactly 1500).

Margin of victory enters through the game score: the winner scores 1 / (1 + e^(−margin / 4)). Home field is worth a rating edge that is estimated each season from the previous two regular seasons only, so nothing looks ahead. Neutral-site games (the 2020 bubble) get no edge.

"Win %" in Games is the pre-game probability the home team wins, converted from Glicko-2's expected score to a true win probability.

2027: enter both scores and press Tab or Enter; ratings update right away. Change a game's type with the selector (playoff games can be added in Add / Import).

Simulate the rest of 2027

How it works

Each simulated season starts from the records so far and plays every standings game (regular season) still without a result. Win probabilities come from the current ratings plus the home edge, converted from Glicko-2's expected score to a true win probability when margin scoring is on. With rating uncertainty on, each season first draws every team's true strength from its rating ± RD, so early in the year the spread of outcomes is wide and it tightens as results come in.

The schedule has 162 games per team; any games missing from it are filled in with random opponents until you add them. Teams are ranked in each league by wins. Ties for a playoff place use the head-to-head record, then the record against the division, then the record within the league, then run differential (the later official steps are skipped and simulated margins are generic). The field is the three division winners plus three wild cards per league. The two best division winners skip the best-of-3 Wild Card Series; then come the best-of-5 Division Series and the best-of-7 League Championship Series and World Series. Odds appear in the Championship odds table.

Import schedule or results

Paste or upload a CSV with the columns Date, Visitor, R, Home, R (one game per line). Plain date,away,home[,awayPts,homePts[,type]] rows work too, and so does a Type or Notes column (Postseason). Team names, nicknames and abbreviations are all understood.

Importing merges: new games are added and scores fill in results for games you already have. Re-import any time to load new results.

Automatic updates

A scheduled job refreshes the schedule and results several times a day and publishes them with this app; the app merges them every time you open it. Results you type yourself are never overwritten, and a result you clear is filled in again from the file.

Glicko-2 parameters

RD at season start is 30 by default and τ is 1.2 (a grid over 216,000 games found start RD 10–30 and τ 0.8–1.6 about equally good: single baseball games are so noisy that ratings move slowly). New franchises start at 350. Margin scales of 2 to 8 runs made almost no difference, so 4 stays.

Model quality

Pre-game predictions of the home team winning, evaluated over every game that feeds the ratings. Log loss of a coin flip is 0.693.

Data and assumptions

Regular seasons 1901–2023 and 2025, and every postseason through 2025, come from the Retrosheet game logs (Chadwick Bureau mirror). The 2024 regular season and all of 2026 come from the MLB Stats API schedule tables (baseballr-data), which match Retrosheet except for a few games a season (suspended games listed twice, home and away swapped at neutral sites). Only American and National League games count: the 1914–15 Federal League, All-Star games and exhibitions are excluded. Games called while level are ties (rare after 1950) and count as half a win; forfeits are scored 9-0. Games at foreign or relocated sites since 1996 (Tokyo, London, Mexico City, Monterrey, Williamsport, relocated series) and the 2020 postseason, except the Wild Card Series, are treated as neutral-site. 1981, 1994–95 and 2020 were shortened by strikes or the pandemic. The information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet. Interested parties may contact Retrosheet at www.retrosheet.org.

Franchise lineage follows the official records: Milwaukee Brewers (1901) → St. Louis Browns → Baltimore Orioles; Baltimore Orioles (1901–02) → New York Highlanders → Yankees; Boston Beaneaters / Doves / Rustlers / Braves / Bees → Milwaukee → Atlanta Braves; Brooklyn Superbas / Dodgers / Robins → Los Angeles Dodgers; New York Giants → San Francisco; Philadelphia → Kansas City → Oakland → Athletics; Washington Senators (1901) → Minnesota Twins; Washington Senators (1961) → Texas Rangers; Seattle Pilots → Milwaukee Brewers; Montréal Expos → Washington Nationals; Houston Colt .45s → Astros. Expansion: Angels and Senators 1961, Mets and Colt .45s 1962, Royals, Pilots, Padres and Expos 1969, Blue Jays and Mariners 1977, Rockies and Marlins 1993, Diamondbacks and Devil Rays 1998. Houston moved from the NL to the AL in 2013 and Milwaukee from the AL to the NL in 1998; the leagues and divisions shown are today's.

Team badges are plain colour tabs with the code, not logos. Source data can contain rare typos in scores or dates.
